article.title: NVIDIA Cosmos3-H-Dreams: Bringing Clinical Surgery to Life Through Generative Simulation

harvestedTerms.summary: NVIDIA introduces Cosmos3-H-Dreams, a real-time generative surgical simulator trained on clinical cholecystectomy recordings that uses world foundation model technology, Self-Forcing distillation, and a streaming inference library (FlashDreams) to enable interactive kinematic control of surgical scenes. The article is technically dense, covering teacher-to-student distillation, causal video generation, KV cache consolidation for long rollouts, and action-conditioned world models for surgical robotics.

article.title: Muse Spark Open, Meta + Apple, Thin and Thick

harvestedTerms.summary: Stratechery paywalled article about Meta releasing an open-source model ('Muse Spark Open') and a surprise partnership with Apple to enable local on-device deployment. The excerpt is almost entirely behind the paywall — only the title, teaser line, and subscription page are visible. No substantive analytical content is accessible.

article.title: Last Week in AI #346 - 719 math manuscripts, 2 Western open models, 1 more safety resignation

harvestedTerms.summary: A news roundup covering: OpenAI releasing 719 math manuscripts from an unreleased frontier model (with governance debate); Mistral and Reflection AI launching large open-weight models pitched as Western rivals to Chinese models; OpenAI safety researcher David Robinson's resignation essay criticizing trial-and-error release culture; and Google opening SynthID Detector publicly while OpenAI adds EU text watermarking.

article.title: Battle Drones—a vibe coded RTS with audio-based multiplayer

harvestedTerms.summary: Simon Willison documents the iterative development of Battle Drones, a browser-based RTS game built almost entirely through vibe coding with Claude Code over 12 major versions. The article showcases audio-based multiplayer (synchronizing game state via sound), Ultracode dynamic workflows that orchestrated subagents for game balancing, and an agent-vs-agent play mode where two LLMs compete. It's primarily a personal project writeup with some interesting embedded concepts around multi-agent simulation and audio data encoding.

Anthropic announcements page covering October–July 2026: new model releases (Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Mythos, Fable 5.1), expansion of verification programs (Cyber, Life Sciences), the Claude Frontier Academy initiative, Model Hardware Standard preview, and various philanthropic/research funding commitments. Primarily a product/news digest with limited terminological novelty.
